title: Build Tool Configuration
description: Learn how build tools work by building a mini module bundler from scratch. Understand dependency graphs, bundling, loaders, and plugins.

steps.title: Dependency graph builder
steps.description: Write a `buildGraph(entryFile)` function that simulates building a dependency graph. Given an entry module ID, recursively resolve dependencies by reading a fake module registry. Return an array of module objects `{ id, code, deps }`. Log the graph to verify.
hints: Use a simple in-memory module registry: { 'moduleA': { code: '...', deps: ['moduleB'] } }
Use a Set to track visited modules and avoid circular dependencies
BFS or DFS traversal — start from the entry module

verification.successMessage: Dependency graph includes entry and all dependencies!
verification.failureMessage: Build the graph from 'entry.js' and include both the entry and its utils dependency.

steps.title: Module bundler
steps.description: Create a `bundle(entryId)` function that takes the dependency graph and produces a single bundle string. The bundle should wrap each module in a function that receives `require`, `module`, and `exports`. Use an IIFE pattern to scope modules.
hints: Build the graph first using buildGraph from step 1
Each module becomes: function(require, module, exports) { ...code... }
The bundle maps module IDs to their factory functions
The entry point is called first with a local require function

verification.successMessage: Bundle wraps modules in factory functions with a custom require system!
verification.failureMessage: The bundle should include factory functions for each module and a require mechanism.

steps.title: Simple minifier
steps.description: Write a `minify(code)` function that performs basic minification: remove single-line comments (`//...`), remove multi-line comments (`/*...*/`), collapse whitespace, and remove unnecessary semicolons before closing braces. Print the original and minified code.

codeTemplate.python:
import re

def minify(code):
    code = re.sub(r'#.*$', '', code, flags=re.MULTILINE)
    code = re.sub(r"'''[\s\S]*?'''", '', code)
    code = re.sub(r'"""[\s\S]*?"""', '', code)
    code = re.sub(r'\n\s+', '\n', code)
    code = re.sub(r'\s+\n', '\n', code)
    code = re.sub(r'[ \t]+', ' ', code)
    code = re.sub(r'\n{3,}', '\n\n', code)
    return code.strip()

original = '''
def hello(name):
    # Greet the user
    msg = "Hello, " + name + "!"
    return msg
'''

minified_code = minify(original)
print('Original chars:', len(original))
print('Minified chars:', len(minified_code))
print('Savings:', round((1 - len(minified_code) / len(original)) * 100, 1), '%')
print('---')
print(minified_code)

verification.failureMessage: Show the character count before and after minification with the percentage saved.

steps.title: Source map generator
steps.description: Create a simple source map that maps minified output positions back to original source positions. Implement `generateSourceMap(original, minified)` that finds corresponding line numbers. Print the mapping as JSON with `{ mappings: [{ originalLine, originalCol, generatedLine, generatedCol }] }`.
hints: Split both original and minified into lines
For each minified line, find which original line(s) it came from
Use a simple algorithm: track character offset and map back to line numbers

verification.successMessage: Source map maps minified lines back to originals!
verification.failureMessage: The source map should include mappings array with line number correspondences.

steps.title: Plugin-style transform pipeline
steps.description: Create a `TransformPipeline` class that accepts an array of plugins. Each plugin is a function `(code) => transformedCode`. Implement `pipeline.process(code)` that runs code through each plugin in order. Create two plugins: `stripLogs` (removes console.log calls) and `addStrict` (adds 'use strict'). Print the result through each stage.
hints: pipeline.process should reduce over the plugins: plugins.reduce((code, plugin) => plugin(code), code)

verification.successMessage: Plugin pipeline processes code through each transform stage!
verification.failureMessage: Print the code after each plugin transformation and the final output.
